title: Tanzanian Coconut Chapati
community: Zanzibar and the Swahili coast — the enriched coastal flatbread
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Chapati ya Nazi — chapati made with coconut milk instead of water, creating a richer, more fragrant, slightly sweeter flatbread with a more tender texture. The coastal version of the everyday chapati — all the layers, twice the flavour.
longDesc: Coconut chapati is the coastal upgrade of Tanzania's everyday flatbread — replacing water with fresh coconut milk produces a chapati that is more tender, more fragrant, and slightly richer than the standard version. On the coast, where coconut milk is as abundant as water, this is simply how chapati is made.
ingredients: 3 tbsp vegetable oil — plus more for cooking
steps: Combine flour, salt, and sugar. Add oil and rub in.
Add coconut milk and water gradually, mixing to a soft dough.
Divide into 8 balls. Roll each thin.
Brush with oil. Fold, brush, fold again into a layered disc. Roll out again.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat 2—3 minutes per side.
Brush with oil during cooking. Keep wrapped.
chefTips: Coconut milk produces a more tender dough than water — do not over-knead.
The fold-and-roll technique creates the flaky layers.
Keep cooked chapatis wrapped — they go hard quickly.
cookingScience: Coconut milk's fat content coats the flour proteins — partially inhibiting gluten development. This produces a more tender, less chewy chapati than water-based dough, while the fat also creates greater flakiness in the layered structure.
storage: Wrap in cloth for 2 days. Freeze 2 months.
culturalNote: Coconut chapati is the coast's most generous gift to the chapati tradition — richer, softer, and more fragrant than the mainland version, it is the bread that makes every coastal Tanzanian meal complete.
